question.problem: A fair six-sided die is rolled $7$ times. What is the probability of getting at least $5$ rolls of $3$ or greater? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
Let the random variable $X$ be equal to the number of times that we get a roll of $3$ or greater.

Here, we have the following information:

- there are $n=7$ rolls

- the probability of getting a roll of $3$ or greater (i.e., a roll of $3,4,5,$ or $6$) on any roll of the die is

$$
p=\frac{4}{6}=\frac{2}{3}
$$

So, $X$ follows a binomial distribution, where $X∼B(7,\frac{2}{3}).$ 

The number of successes of a binomial random variable has the probability mass function

$$
P(X=x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{x}){p}^{x}(1-p)^{n-x},
$$

where $n$ is the number of experiments, and $p$ is the probability of success on each experiment.

Substituting the above information into the formula for probability mass function, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=x) & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{x}){(\frac{2}{3})}^{x}{(1-\frac{2}{3})}^{7-x} \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{x}){(\frac{2}{3})}^{x}{(\frac{1}{3})}^{7-x}.\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find the probability of getting a "success" (i.e., a roll of $3$ or greater) on at least $5$ rolls. So, we compute

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\ge 5) & =P(X=5)+P(X=6)+P(X=7) \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{5}){(\frac{2}{3})}^{5}{(\frac{1}{3})}^{7-5}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{6}){(\frac{2}{3})}^{6}{(\frac{1}{3})}^{7-6}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{7}){(\frac{2}{3})}^{7}{(\frac{1}{3})}^{7-7} \\  & =21{(\frac{2}{3})}^{5}{(\frac{1}{3})}^{2}+7{(\frac{2}{3})}^{6}(\frac{1}{3})+1{(\frac{2}{3})}^{7} \\  & =0.571\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
